name: What should I ask a contractor before hiring them for an attached ADU?

mainEntity.name: Which experience, documents, and construction details matter most when selecting a builder for an attached ADU project?
mainEntity.text: Which experience, documents, and construction details matter most when selecting a builder for an attached ADU project?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hiring the right contractor is especially important for attached ADUs because these projects depend on careful coordination with the existing house. Homeowners should ask whether the builder has completed similar attached additions, not just detached accessory units or general remodels. Key topics include structural tie-ins, fire-rated separation, utility upgrades, permit handling, dust and occupant protection, and how the contractor manages work in or near an occupied home. It is also smart to ask how change orders are priced, who communicates with the designer and engineer, and what happens if hidden conditions appear after demolition. A strong contractor should be able to explain realistic timelines and identify the most likely project risks before construction begins. If the answers are vague or overly optimistic, that is usually a warning sign. For attached ADUs, the best choice is not simply the lowest bid; it is the team that understands how to build cleanly into an existing house without creating avoidable surprises.
acceptedAnswer.description: Ask about attached ADU experience, structural tie-ins, permit coordination, utility upgrades, and how they handle existing-home protection during construction. A good contractor should also explain realistic timelines, allowances, change-order policy, and who coordinates with the designer and engineer.
